deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematical derivation. It is a page of anatomical notes and measurements, written with the sheet turned upside down relative to the scan. It belongs to the material for Riemann's last, unfinished work, 'Mechanik des Ohres' (written 1866, edited posthumously by Henle), which the bundle name 'R.Ohr' points to.

The page holds three things.
(a) A heading '13/4'. This is most plausibly a date (13 April, likely 1866) or a specimen or ear number.
(b) Two blocks of measurements:
  - 'D. [8?] mm, Tief[e] 1½ –'. Probably the diameter (Durchmesser) of a roughly circular structure, about 8 mm, and its depth, 1½ mm.
  - 'Breit[e] 1½ mm, Tief[e] 2 mm'. A width of 1½ mm and a depth of 2 mm.
(c) Two freehand sketches of roughly circular or oval outlines. Each has a line running from near the rim toward the centre, plus a small knob-like detail. One sketch is labelled 0,4 and the other 0,5, with a leader line to one outline. These are likely values in mm.

My tentative interpretation: the sketches show the tympanic membrane seen from outside, with the manubrium (handle) of the malleus running to the umbo. A diameter of about 8–9 mm and a funnel depth of about 1.5–2 mm fit the standard anatomy of the drum membrane well. On that reading, 0,4 and 0,5 might be small offsets or thicknesses read off the specimens. An alternative is that the figures are dimensions of ossicle parts, for example the malleus–incus joint surfaces that Riemann discusses.

These are empirical data. Riemann presumably intended them as inputs to his mechanical analysis of how the ossicle chain transmits sound. No computation is carried out on this page.
errors: No derivations are present, so there are no mathematical errors to report. The readings of the numbers are uncertain (especially '8' and the labels 0,4 / 0,5), so any numerical interpretation is provisional.

results.what: Anatomical measurements (diameter about 8 mm, depth 1½–2 mm, width 1½ mm, small dimensions 0.4 and 0.5) and sketches, probably of the tympanic membrane with the malleus handle or of ossicle structures.
results.modern_name: Morphometry of the middle ear (tympanic membrane / ossicles)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 19th-century otological anatomy (e.g. Helmholtz 1868, Henle, Politzer)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine anatomical measurements and sketches in preparation for Riemann's known work on the mechanics of the ear. The page contains no mathematics and no novel result.

checkable.asserts: Depth-to-diameter ratio of the funnel-shaped structure if D = 8 mm and depth = 1.5 mm (= 3/16).
The approximate inclination angle (about 20.6 degrees) of a cone of diameter 8 mm and depth 1.5 mm. This is a sanity check that the figures fit a shallow tympanic-membrane cone.

transcription_corrections: The page is written upside down; the image must be rotated 180° to read it.
'D. 8[?] mm' is probably an abbreviation for Durchmesser (diameter) or similar. The digit after 'D.' is uncertain; 8 is plausible, but it may be overwritten.
The first block's 'Tief 1½ —' has a dash, presumably meaning mm or 'same unit'.
The sketch labels are '0,4' (lower/oval sketch) and '0,5' (upper/round sketch, with a leader line).
